claims.statement: For a finite ordinary tree U rooted at r, adjoining r-s-v gives I(T;z)=(1+z)I(U;z)+zI(U-r;z), alpha(T)=alpha(U)+1, I(T-v;z)=I(U;z)+zI(U-r;z), and the new leaf contribution is Delta_(p-1)(I(U)-I(U-r)).
claims.scope: Exact for every finite ordinary tree U and distinguished vertex r; the selector is the strict test Delta_p(T-v)<0 and the contribution uses the original new leaf v and support s.
claims.reason: retained: partitioning independent sets by whether the new support s is selected proves both polynomial identities; the original deletion sets for v are U and U-r, and the independence-number formula follows from the same partition.

claims.statement: The pendant-P2 recurrence alone does not establish the complete favorable-leaf aggregate inequality at the exact shell |T|=2p+2; first-descent transfer, every strict selector value, and comparison of the complete original-leaf sum remain unproved by this recurrence.
claims.scope: The recurrence-based argument for the registered first-order shell, preserving the exact primary guards, original supports, and one summand per selected original leaf; this is a proof-gap diagnosis, not a verdict on the shell assertion.
claims.reason: retained_narrowed: the recurrence establishes order, alpha, and the new-leaf term, but neither transfers x or the strict selector for all retained leaves nor bounds the full recalculated sum. The K_(1,4) diagnostic confirms x can change (2 to 3), but is ineligible at every p and is not a shell refutation.

limitations: No eligible first-order-shell refutation or universal shell proof is established.
